suggestions.reason: The engagement clause as drafted imposes a unilateral acceptance obligation on Columbia Capital Management as Consultant while articulating no express corresponding obligation on the City, most critically the obligation to pay for the Services performed. This exposes Columbia Capital Management to the commercial risk of performing under the Agreement without an unambiguous payment commitment in the foundational engagement provision. Additionally, the reference to "the services described in this Agreement" uses an uncapitalized, undefined term, creating interpretive ambiguity as to the precise scope of Columbia Capital Management's performance obligations, which a counterparty could later exploit to dispute whether particular work falls within the agreed scope.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the services described in this Agreement and Consultant accepts that engagement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the Services described in this Agreement, and in consideration thereof, the City shall pay Consultant the fees set forth in this Agreement. Consultant accepts that engagement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Exhibit A uses the phrase "Consultant's scope of services shall include:" — an open-ended formulation that exposes Columbia Capital Management to scope creep, because The City could argue that analogous or related work is implicitly captured within the Contract Services without triggering the supplemental agreement mechanism. Without an express statement that services not described in Exhibit A fall outside the Contract Services, Columbia Capital Management bears the risk of performing uncompensated work or facing a dispute as to whether a task was always within scope. These two deficiencies together undermine the written-amendment protection in the final sentence, which is Columbia Capital Management's primary commercial safeguard against performing unremunerated additional work.
suggestions.original_text: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform only those services ("Contract Services") expressly described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference; any services not expressly described in Exhibit A are outside the scope of the Contract Services. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City's request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

suggestions.reason: Section 3 as drafted does nothing more than redirect payment to Exhibit A, leaving every operative payment mechanic—invoicing procedure, payment due date, late-payment remedy, and expense treatment—entirely unaddressed in the Agreement itself. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates direct financial exposure: without a stated payment deadline the City faces no contractual obligation to pay within any particular period, and without a late-payment interest provision Columbia Capital Management has no leverage to enforce timely remittance short of litigation. The absence of any expense framework means Columbia Capital Management could be left bearing unrecovered costs with no contractual basis for reimbursement. These gaps should also be reflected in Exhibit A if not resolved here, and any late-payment interest rate added must be consistent with applicable statutory limits under governing law.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement. The Consultant shall submit invoices to the City on a monthly basis, and the City shall remit payment within thirty (30) days of receipt of each invoice. Reimbursable expenses shall be as specified in Exhibit A. Any undisputed amounts remaining unpaid after thirty (30) days of receipt shall accrue interest at the rate set forth in Exhibit A, or if not specified therein, at the maximum rate permitted by applicable law.

suggestions.reason: The current clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to significant financial and reputational risk because it allows the City to terminate "for cause" on sixty (60) days' notice without first providing Columbia Capital Management any opportunity to cure an alleged breach, meaning the City could characterize any minor or disputed non-conformance as "cause" and terminate without affording CCM a chance to remedy it. The term "cause" is also left undefined, giving the City unfettered discretion to invoke a for-cause termination—which could carry adverse reputational consequences for Columbia Capital Management—when a termination for convenience might otherwise apply. The survival clause fails to expressly preserve CCM's right to payment for Contract Services performed prior to termination, creating a risk that this payment obligation lapses upon termination despite the express language in the clause itself, and no dispute resolution provision is listed as surviving, which could leave CCM without a clear mechanism to enforce unpaid amounts.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days’ written notice for convenience or cause upon written notice to Consultant. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days’ written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice to Consultant, with termination taking effect upon expiration of such sixty (60) day period. The City may terminate this Agreement for cause upon written notice to Consultant specifying in reasonable detail the alleged material breach; provided that Consultant shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of such notice to cure the identified material breach, and termination shall take effect only if such breach remains uncured at the expiration of that thirty (30) day cure period. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days' written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity, insurance, payment for Contract Services performed prior to termination, and dispute resolution shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the compliance obligation imposed on Consultant contains no reference to anti-bribery and anti-corruption requirements, no obligation on Consultant to notify Columbia Capital Management if a legal violation affecting the Contract Services occurs, and no supply-chain conduct standard addressing forced labour or human trafficking. These gaps expose Columbia Capital Management to reputational, regulatory, and financial liability arising from Consultant's conduct that Columbia Capital Management could not detect or mitigate in time, because Consultant bears no duty to disclose a breach. The absence of these obligations is particularly material given that the indemnification running in favour of the City depends entirely on the breadth of the underlying compliance obligation — a narrowly scoped compliance clause correspondingly narrows the class of indemnifiable violations.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, including without limitation applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and forced labour and human trafficking laws, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall promptly notify the City in writing if Consultant becomes aware of any violation of applicable law or regulation that affects the Contract Services. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules
suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted limits Consultant's compliance obligations to a narrow set of Kansas-specific anti-discrimination statutes, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed where Consultant breaches anti-bribery, anti-corruption, or anti-forced-labor laws applicable to the engagement, none of which are addressed. Because there is also no obligation on Consultant to notify Columbia Capital Management upon becoming aware of any such breach, Columbia Capital Management could face regulatory scrutiny, reputational harm, or liability derived from Consultant's conduct without any contractual mechanism to compel timely disclosure or take remedial action.
suggestions.original_text: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.), the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.), and applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and anti-forced-labor laws, and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age. Consultant shall promptly notify Columbia Capital Management in writing upon becoming aware of any breach of the foregoing that affects this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The insurance obligation is limited to "the duration of this Agreement," leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to claims arising from the Consultant's work that surface only after termination or expiration — a material gap in a professional services context where latent errors, omissions, or professional negligence may not manifest until well after project completion. Additionally, the clause contains no statement that the insurance coverages required do not cap or otherwise limit the Consultant's total liability to Columbia Capital Management, which creates a risk that the Consultant will characterize its insurance policy limits as the ceiling on its indemnification or damages exposure under this Agreement. These two deficiencies, taken together, could significantly undermine Columbia Capital Management's ability to recover its full losses from a Consultant default or negligence claim.
suggestions.original_text: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.
suggestions.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement and for a period of not less than three (3) years following the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The required insurance coverages shall not be construed to limit or otherwise affect the Consultant's liability to The City under this Agreement. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement's execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

suggestions.reason: The indemnification provision runs exclusively in favor of the City, with no reciprocal obligation on the City to indemnify Columbia Capital Management for claims arising from the City's own negligence or intentional misconduct, exposing Columbia Capital Management to unilateral financial risk on a project where both parties bear potential fault. The absence of defense control rights and a settlement consent mechanism means Columbia Capital Management could be compelled to fund or be bound by a defense strategy or settlement it had no authority to direct or approve. No mitigation obligation is imposed on the City, leaving Columbia Capital Management potentially responsible for losses the City could have reasonably limited. The clause expressly states it is not constrained by other indemnification provisions elsewhere in the Agreement yet is entirely silent on its relationship to any liability cap, creating a material risk that Columbia Capital Management's indemnity exposure is effectively uncapped.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, (a) Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, and (b) City shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Consultant, its officers, employees, and agents, in each case from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, to the extent caused by the negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of such indemnifying party, its subcontractors, or anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant's services. The indemnifying party shall control the defense of any indemnified claim, and no settlement shall be effected without the indemnified party's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. The party seeking indemnification shall provide written notice within ten (10) days of becoming aware of any such claim, cooperate with the indemnifying party in the defense thereof, and take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate its losses. Each party's indemnification obligations under this Section are subject to any limitation of liability set forth in this Agreement, except to the extent arising from a party's fraud or willful misconduct.

suggestions.reason: The continue-performance obligation in this clause falls exclusively on Columbia Capital Management as Consultant, with no reciprocal requirement that the City continue making payments during a dispute, exposing Columbia Capital Management to the material financial risk of providing unrecompensed services while a claim remains unresolved. The clause also identifies no governing law and no specific forum, instead permitting whichever party initiates a claim to pursue "such steps as it deems necessary," meaning the City could unilaterally select an inconvenient or costly forum without limitation, leaving Columbia Capital Management without a predictable dispute resolution framework it can rely upon. The absence of a defined negotiation period and any carve-out for emergency injunctive or equitable relief further compromises Columbia Capital Management's ability to protect its rights in time-critical situations.
suggestions.original_text: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement should first be addressed by negotiations between the parties. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, the party initiating the claim that is the basis of the dispute shall be free to take such steps as it deems necessary to protect its interest; provided, however, that notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement shall first be addressed by good-faith negotiations for no fewer than thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute within such period, either party may pursue its claims before a court of competent jurisdiction. Notwithstanding any such dispute, each party shall continue to perform its obligations under this Agreement, including the City's obligation to make payments when due; provided that either party may seek emergency injunctive or equitable relief without first exhausting the foregoing negotiation period. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which the City is located.

suggestions.reason: The Representations clause as drafted is limited to a single anti-collusion pricing statement and fails to include any performance standard, any warranty against third-party intellectual property infringement, or any remedy available to Columbia Capital Management upon breach. Without a performance standard, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual baseline against which to measure or enforce deficient service delivery. The absence of an IP non-infringement warranty exposes Columbia Capital Management to third-party infringement claims arising from deliverables it receives and relies upon, with no corresponding contractual recourse against the Provider, and the omission of any breach remedy leaves Columbia Capital Management without an express right to re-performance or a refund when the Provider fails to meet its obligations.
suggestions.original_text: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.
suggestions.suggested_fix: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion. Provider further warrants that: (i) the Services shall be performed with reasonable professional skill and care; (ii) the Services and Deliverables shall not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights; and (iii) upon breach of any warranty in this Section, Provider shall, at Columbia Capital Management's election, re-perform the non-conforming Services or refund the fees paid for such Services.

suggestions.reason: The current provision imposes only a narrow anti-kickback warranty on the Consultant, with no mutual representation by either party of compliance with applicable laws. This creates a material gap for Columbia Capital Management: if the Consultant breaches a law beyond the City's gratuities policy—such as employment, licensing, or professional services regulations—Columbia Capital Management has no express contractual warranty to enforce and no corresponding representation from the Consultant on which to predicate a breach claim. The provision also imposes no reciprocal compliance obligation on Columbia Capital Management, which could appear asymmetric if the clause is later scrutinized in a dispute or regulatory context.
suggestions.original_text: The Consultant has not violated, is not violating, and promises that it will not violate the City’s policy of prohibition against gratuities and kickbacks.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party represents that it has not violated, is not violating, and will not violate any applicable laws, including the City's policy of prohibition against gratuities and kickbacks.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation is unilateral: only the Consultant warrants its power and authority to execute and perform the Agreement, leaving no corresponding representation from Columbia Capital Management. This asymmetry creates an enforceability risk for Columbia Capital Management — if the Consultant later challenges the Agreement's validity on the basis that Columbia Capital Management's signatory lacked authority, there is no contractual warranty from Columbia Capital Management to anchor mutual enforceability. A bilateral authority representation is market-standard in professional services agreements and protects Columbia Capital Management's ability to hold the Consultant to its obligations.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party represents and warrants that it has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement, and that the individuals who have signed this Agreement on its behalf have the legal power, right, and authority to make this Agreement and to bind such party.

suggestions.reason: The warranty standards in this clause — "state of the art procedures and techniques" and "recognized professional standards prevalent in their field" — are undefined and insufficiently objective, exposing Columbia Capital Management to significant enforcement risk if the Consultant delivers substandard work and disputes the applicable benchmark. Because neither phrase refers to an identifiable, objectively determinable standard, a court would likely require extrinsic evidence to resolve any dispute, undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to hold the Consultant accountable. Additionally, while the clause imposes warranty obligations on the Consultant, it provides Columbia Capital Management with no express remedy upon a breach of those warranties, leaving the Consultant's re-performance or cost-remediation obligations entirely implicit and legally uncertain.
suggestions.original_text: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement, shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and service performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall conform to or exceed the professional standards generally accepted in the relevant professional field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of current industry-standard procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services. In the event of any breach of the foregoing warranties, Columbia Capital Management shall be entitled to require the Consultant to re-perform the non-conforming work promptly and at no additional cost to Columbia Capital Management.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the Assignment clause imposes consent obligations exclusively on the Consultant while placing no restriction on the City's ability to assign the Agreement freely, exposing Columbia Capital Management to having its contractual relationship transferred to an unknown or adverse counterparty without recourse. The City's consent right contains no reasonableness standard or response period, meaning the City may arbitrarily withhold consent to a commercially necessary assignment — such as an affiliate restructuring or corporate acquisition — causing material operational disruption to Columbia Capital Management. Additionally, the clause contains no continuing liability mechanism to bind an assigning party after transfer, no affiliate or M&A carve-out for Consultant, and no change of control termination right, leaving Columbia Capital Management without protection if the City itself is acquired or merged.
suggestions.original_text: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant without the prior written consent of the City. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant, whether consented to or not.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by either party without the prior written consent of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that Consultant may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, so long as the assigning party remains liable for all obligations hereunder. Either party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the other party if the other party undergoes a change of control. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the permitted successors and assigns of each party.

suggestions.reason: The notices clause sets out Columbia Capital Management's contact details but contains no mechanism by which either party may update those details over time. Without a change-of-details procedure, any notice sent by the counterparty to a stale address could be deemed validly delivered, exposing Columbia Capital Management to missed legal notices, cure-period deadlines, or termination notices without actual receipt. A brief written-notice requirement for address changes is a standard, low-cost protection that eliminates this operational gap.
suggestions.original_text: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204
suggestions.suggested_fix: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204. Either party may change its notice details by providing written notice of such change to the other party, which change shall be effective five (5) Business Days following receipt of such written notice.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to three material gaps that could be used against it. First, the absence of any statement that Consultant controls the manner and means of performing the Services weakens the independent contractor characterization, increasing the risk that a court or taxing authority reclassifies Columbia Capital Management as an employee — an outcome that would trigger the existing indemnification obligation to defend the City against resulting employment tax and benefits liability. Second, the clause addresses only Consultant's tax and withholding obligations while omitting any reciprocal statement that each party bears responsibility for its own personnel's compensation, benefits, and employment taxes, leaving that allocation ambiguous and potentially shifting implied obligations onto Columbia Capital Management. Third, without an express provision that neither party may bind or create obligations on behalf of the other, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual protection against the City purporting to act as its agent or committing it to third-party liabilities.
suggestions.original_text: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor who controls the manner and means of performing the Services hereunder. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Each party shall be solely responsible for all compensation, benefits, taxes, and withholdings applicable to its own respective personnel. Neither party shall have authority to bind or create any obligation on behalf of the other party. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law
suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 17 addresses only the Kansas Cash-Basis Law funding mechanism and is entirely silent on broader legal compliance obligations, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no contractual protection against the City's potential violations of anti-bribery or anti-corruption laws, no right to receive notice if the City breaches any applicable law materially affecting this Agreement, no allocation of compliance costs if the law changes, and no supply-chain labour standards framework. The practical risk to Columbia Capital Management is significant: absent a notification obligation, Columbia Capital Management could unknowingly continue performing under an Agreement that is legally compromised on the City's side, exposing Columbia Capital Management to reputational and regulatory liability with no contractual recourse. The lack of a change-in-law cost allocation further means Columbia Capital Management could be required to absorb unforeseen compliance expenditures without the ability to seek an equitable adjustment from the City.
suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 17. Compliance with Applicable Laws. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. Each party shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations governing its performance under this Agreement, including those relating to anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and the prohibition of forced labour and child labour in its operations and supply chain. Each party shall promptly notify the other party in writing upon becoming aware of any breach of applicable law that materially affects this Agreement, and any additional costs of compliance arising solely from a change in applicable law shall be borne by the party upon whom such obligation is legally imposed. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City's current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "legal actions" is undefined and ambiguous — a court could interpret it to cover only litigation commenced by filing a civil complaint, potentially excluding equitable proceedings, emergency injunctive relief, or other proceedings that Columbia Capital Management may need to initiate to protect its rights under this Agreement. Similarly, the formulation "arising out of this Agreement" is narrower than market-standard drafting and could be construed to exclude tortious or statutory claims that relate to, but do not strictly arise under, the Agreement's terms, creating a forum-shopping risk where the counterparty contests venue for claims Columbia Capital Management seeks to bring. Together, these ambiguities expose Columbia Capital Management to threshold jurisdictional disputes before the merits of any dispute are even reached.
suggestions.original_text: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any legal actions arising out of this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any actions, suits, or proceedings arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas.

suggestions.reason: The current provision is a bare choice-of-law clause that does nothing more than designate Kansas law; it is wholly silent on forum selection, pre-dispute escalation, mutual submission to jurisdiction, urgent relief, and continued performance obligations during a dispute. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates serious practical exposure: the absence of an agreed forum means the counterparty could commence proceedings in a hostile or inconvenient jurisdiction, forcing Columbia Capital Management to litigate venue before addressing the merits, while the lack of a pre-dispute escalation step removes a valuable cost-control mechanism that benefits Columbia Capital Management as a sophisticated capital management firm likely to prefer commercial resolution over immediate litigation. The absence of a continued-performance obligation during disputes is equally critical, as it could allow the counterparty to suspend its Services obligations the moment a dispute arises, leaving Columbia Capital Management without recourse or operational continuity.
suggestions.original_text: Section 19. Governing Law. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 19. Governing Law; Dispute Resolution. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas. Prior to commencing formal proceedings, the parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute through senior executive negotiation for a period of thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute from either party. Any unresolved dispute shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the State of Kansas, to which both parties irrevocably submit. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek urgent injunctive or equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction without first completing the negotiation period. Each party shall continue to perform its obligations under this Agreement pending final resolution of any dispute.

suggestions.reason: The automatic reformation mechanism states only that an invalid provision shall be "reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements," without specifying the standard or scope of that reformation. This ambiguity exposes Columbia Capital Management to a risk that a court or counterparty could argue for a reformation that departs materially from the originally negotiated intent, potentially replacing a provision favorable to Columbia Capital Management with one that is not. Without an express requirement that reformation be limited to the minimum change necessary and be as close as possible to the parties' original intent, the clause provides no anchor against an expansive or commercially disadvantageous rewrite of an invalidated term.
suggestions.original_text: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended to the minimum extent necessary to conform to applicable legal requirements while preserving the original intent of the parties as closely as possible, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted protects against implied waivers arising from inaction and correctly requires waivers to be in writing, but it omits the standard market protection that a waiver of one specific breach or right does not operate as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach of the same or any other provision. Without this language, a counterparty could argue that Columbia Capital Management's written waiver of a particular default—for example, a missed milestone or a reporting obligation—creates a broader precedent affecting Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce the same or related provisions in the future. This gap materially undermines Columbia Capital Management's contractual enforcement position across the Agreement wherever waivers may be granted in the course of an ongoing professional services relationship.
suggestions.original_text: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party. No waiver of any breach of any provision of this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of any prior, concurrent, or subsequent breach of the same or any other provision hereof.

suggestions.reason: The current clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to three interrelated risks: first, "signed by both parties" does not specify that signatories must be authorized representatives, meaning an unauthorized employee's signature could be argued to bind Columbia Capital Management to an amendment it never sanctioned; second, the clause does not expressly extend to schedules or exhibits, leaving open an argument that attachments integral to the Agreement's commercial terms can be varied outside the amendment process; and third, the absence of an anti-oral-modification provision means that a counterparty could assert that subsequent emails, verbal exchanges, or course of dealing altered Columbia Capital Management's rights or obligations without a formal written amendment.
suggestions.original_text: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement, including any schedules or exhibits hereto, may not be amended except by a written instrument signed by an authorized representative of each party. No oral agreement, course of conduct, or course of dealing shall constitute or effect an amendment hereto.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this survivorship clause exclusively enumerates Consultant's obligations—Insurance and Indemnification—while making no express provision for Columbia Capital Management's own material post-termination rights, such as confidentiality protections, intellectual property ownership, and accrued payment entitlements. Because the clause is silent on those rights, a counterparty could argue that Columbia Capital Management's corresponding protections lapse upon termination, leaving the firm exposed with no enforceable remedy. The open-ended catch-all—"any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination"—compounds this risk by being sufficiently ambiguous that two courts could reach opposite conclusions on whether a given provision survives, undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce critical post-termination rights. Indefinite survival of Indemnification obligations without any temporal boundary also creates unlimited forward-looking exposure with no certainty of closure for either party.
suggestions.original_text: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant’s obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant's obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and Columbia Capital Management's rights with respect to Confidentiality, Intellectual Property ownership, and any payment obligations accrued prior to the effective date of termination, together with any other provisions that expressly state they survive or that by their nature are intended to survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the compliance covenant requires Columbia Capital Management to act in accordance with "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" — a phrase that is undefined, unbounded in scope, and could be construed to impose obligations under any conceivable body of law, exposing Columbia Capital Management to unlimited liability for non-compliance with standards that are unknowable at the time of execution. This open-ended formulation creates a material risk that the City could invoke any statutory or regulatory violation, however tangential, as a breach of this Agreement, without any corresponding obligation on the City to provide the information and cooperation Columbia Capital Management requires to perform. The absence of any reciprocal obligation on the City's part further skews the clause against Columbia Capital Management in a commercially unjustifiable way.
suggestions.original_text: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the “Accounts”). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the "Accounts"). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all applicable laws and regulations governing investment advisory services. The City shall provide Consultant with all reasonably necessary information and cooperation to enable Consultant to perform its obligations under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The "prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims" standard imports ERISA-derived language without anchoring it to investment management specifically, leaving the operative benchmark sufficiently vague that the Consultant could dispute whether any particular conduct fell below it. For Columbia Capital Management, this ambiguity is commercially material: a Consultant managing client assets could invoke the imprecision of "enterprise of like character" or "such matters" to resist liability for underperformance or conflicts of interest, undermining the enforceability of the fiduciary obligation that this clause is intended to establish. Anchoring the standard explicitly to investment management industry practice removes that interpretive escape and gives Columbia Capital Management a clearer foundation for any breach claim.
suggestions.original_text: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent investment manager acting in a like capacity and familiar with investment management matters would use in the management of assets of like character and with like aims, consistent with applicable investment management industry standards. Any failure by Consultant to meet this standard shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The obligation to provide "periodic" portfolio reporting is undefined in both frequency and format, exposing Columbia Capital Management to disputed performance claims if the City later asserts that its reporting cadence was insufficient to satisfy the contractual standard. Without a specified reporting interval, Columbia Capital Management has no objective benchmark against which its compliance can be measured, creating material liability risk in the event of a disagreement or dispute with the City. This ambiguity also invites scope creep, as the City could demand reporting more frequently than Columbia Capital Management's operational model contemplates, without any contractual basis to resist such demands.
suggestions.original_text: Providing periodic portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Providing no less than quarterly portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "ad hoc reporting and other routine requests related to investment management" is materially ambiguous, as it sets no boundaries on the type, volume, or frequency of work Columbia Capital Management is obligated to perform, exposing it to unconstrained scope creep and fee disputes with the City. Additionally, the clause lacks any triggering condition specifying when this obligation arises — there is no requirement that the City make a formal or written request — meaning Columbia Capital Management could face claims of non-performance for requests it was never properly notified of. Left unaddressed, the City could characterize any number of additional services as "routine requests" and demand performance without supplemental compensation or defined scope parameters.
suggestions.original_text: Providing the City with general market information, ad hoc reporting and other routine requests related to investment management.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Providing the City with general market information, ad hoc reporting, and other routine requests reasonably related to investment management, upon written request by the City.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the City retains an unrestricted, unilateral right to issue or amend investment policy guidelines "from time to time" with no advance notice requirement and no transition period, while simultaneously Columbia Capital Management bears sole discretion — and by implication sole accountability — for every investment decision made in the Accounts. This creates a material compliance and liability trap for Columbia Capital Management: guidelines could change without warning after investment positions have been initiated, exposing Columbia Capital Management to breach claims for decisions that were fully compliant at the time they were executed. The absence of any notice requirement or prospective-only effective date for amended guidelines also directly contradicts the grant of "sole discretion," because that discretion cannot be meaningfully exercised if the governing parameters may shift retroactively or without adequate opportunity to adjust the portfolio. This provision should be read alongside any indemnification or standard-of-care clause in the Agreement, as uncorrected it could undermine Columbia Capital Management's ability to rely on a good-faith compliance defence.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City upon reasonable advance written notice, and any new or amended guidelines shall become binding on Consultant only on a prospective basis following receipt of such notice; provided that Consultant shall not be liable for investment decisions made in conformity with the guidelines in effect at the time such decisions were executed. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.

suggestions.reason: The word "Timely" imposes no objectively enforceable deadline on the City, meaning Columbia Capital Management has no contractual basis to compel delivery of account balances, statements, and interest-earned data within any determinable period. Without a fixed delivery schedule, the City could withhold or delay this information indefinitely, directly impairing Columbia Capital Management's ability to determine required liquidity levels and execute the investment plan in accordance with its mandate. The resulting ambiguity would require extrinsic evidence to resolve in a dispute, exposing Columbia Capital Management to both performance risk and professional liability for investment decisions made on stale or incomplete financial data.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Within five (5) Business Days of each calendar month-end, provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the City's obligation is only to "respond to" Columbia Capital Management's transfer requests, which does not require the City to actually execute or comply with those requests — a mere acknowledgment or even a refusal would technically satisfy this language. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates direct operational and financial risk: if the City declines or delays acting on a transfer instruction, Columbia Capital Management's ability to implement the investment plan could be frustrated, yet the City would not be in breach of this provision. Without a clear duty to execute timely transfers, Columbia Capital Management may also face reputational and liability exposure for investment underperformance caused entirely by the City's inaction.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant’s requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City’s various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request and with reasonable notice, promptly comply with and execute Consultant's requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City's various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes an obligation on the City to instruct the Custodian but sets no timeframe for doing so, exposing Columbia Capital Management to securities settlement failures and associated financial liability if the City delays instructions after trade execution. The phrase "copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant" is undefined and ambiguous — it is unclear what form or standard these documents must meet, creating a risk that the City or Custodian disputes the adequacy of Columbia Capital Management's confirmations and uses that ambiguity to deflect responsibility for a failed settlement onto Columbia Capital Management. Additionally, the statutory reference to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) is cited as a trigger without articulating within the clause the operative condition that activates the City's duty, reducing enforceability should the City contest the instruction obligation.
suggestions.original_text: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1), the City shall, within one (1) Business Day following receipt of written trade confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant, instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with such written trade confirmations.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains no obligation on Consultant to disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest to Columbia Capital Management, leaving Columbia Capital Management entirely dependent on Consultant's unilaterally declared internal policy rather than a contractual commitment. As a practical matter, Columbia Capital Management cannot monitor, assess, or respond to a conflict it is never informed of, and the acknowledgment that the policy "may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time" operates as a blanket advance waiver of harm without any corresponding right to notice or remedy. Without a disclosure obligation, Columbia Capital Management bears the financial risk of foregone investment opportunities and constrained portfolio performance with no visibility into when or why those limitations are being applied. This gap also creates a risk that undisclosed conflicts could accumulate over the term of the Agreement without Columbia Capital Management having any contractual basis to demand transparency or take corrective action.
suggestions.original_text: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an “Issuer Client”), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time. Consultant shall promptly disclose to the City in writing any actual or potential conflict of interest that may affect the City's Accounts, including any new Issuer Client relationship that could restrict investment opportunities available to the City, and shall provide such disclosure prior to or as soon as reasonably practicable after the conflict arises.

suggestions.reason: The clause permits the City to amend Schedule X — the foundational document governing which individuals may direct Columbia Capital Management with respect to the Accounts — "at any time" with no defined notice period before the amendment takes effect. This exposes Columbia Capital Management to material operational and compliance risk: without minimum advance notice, Columbia Capital Management may act on instructions from individuals whose authority has been silently revoked, or may face conflicting direction from newly authorized personnel before it has had any reasonable opportunity to update its internal authorization and trading protocols. Additionally, "Schedule X" appears to be an unfilled placeholder, leaving the authorization framework itself unanchored to any completed exhibit; Columbia Capital Management should require that this schedule be identified and attached before execution. The absence of a specified notice period also creates an enforcement ambiguity that a court would be required to resolve through extrinsic evidence.
suggestions.original_text: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing by the City upon at least ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice to Consultant, with any such amendment becoming effective only upon the expiration of such notice period. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.

suggestions.reason: The Management Fees clause as drafted exposes Columbia Capital Management to material financial risk on multiple fronts: it sets no payment due date, provides no mechanism for Columbia Capital Management to dispute an erroneous invoice, and contains no protection against unilateral fee changes, leaving Consultant free to assert revised rates without written agreement. Without a dispute right, Columbia Capital Management could face a claim of default simply by withholding a contested amount, and without a fixed-fee covenant, the 0.20% rate has no contractual anchor against modification. The absence of an expenses carve-out beyond the "sole compensation" recital also leaves open the risk of Consultant attempting to charge additional costs not separately approved.
suggestions.original_text: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000; such fee rate is fixed and may not be modified except by written amendment executed by both parties. Invoices shall be delivered to Columbia Capital Management within fifteen (15) days following the end of each quarter and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Columbia Capital Management may dispute any invoice in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, and disputed amounts shall be withheld pending written resolution without constituting a default; undisputed amounts remain due by the applicable due date. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement, and no additional expenses shall be charged to Columbia Capital Management without its prior written consent. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies" is ambiguous for Columbia Capital Management as Consultant because "in respect of" is an imprecise connector that a court could read narrowly to cover only the ministerial act of casting proxy votes, while leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to claims arising from proxy-related advice, recommendations, or omissions furnished during the engagement. A counterparty could plausibly argue that the exclusion is limited to the act of voting itself and does not extend to any ancillary proxy-related conduct, creating an avoidable litigation exposure for Columbia Capital Management. Replacing the vague connector with precise causal language eliminates that interpretive gap and squarely protects Columbia Capital Management from any claim connected to proxy voting.
suggestions.original_text: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies and Consultant shall have no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies and Consultant shall have no responsibility of any kind arising out of or in connection with the voting of proxies.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause records only Consultant's regulatory registration status and form-delivery obligation, leaving Columbia Capital Management without any enforceable performance standard, a compliance warranty broader than adviser registration, protection against third-party intellectual property claims arising from the Services, a defined warranty period, or any stated remedy if Consultant's representations prove false. The absence of these elements means that if Consultant performs the Services negligently, delivers infringing work product, or violates applicable law, Columbia Capital Management has no express contractual basis to demand re-performance or a refund and bears the full financial and legal exposure. The warranty period gap is particularly acute because without a stated period the representations may be read as point-in-time statements only, eliminating Columbia Capital Management's ability to invoke them for breaches discovered during engagement.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant (i) is registered as an “investment adviser” under the Investment  Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the “Consultants Act”); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; and (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant represents and warrants that, throughout the term of this Agreement, it (i) is registered as an "investment adviser" under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the "Consultants Act") and complies with all applicable laws; (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time Consultant ceases being so registered; (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act; (iv) will perform the Services with the professional skill and care of a qualified investment adviser; and (v) the Services and any deliverables will not infringe any third party's intellectual property rights. Upon breach of any of the foregoing warranties, Consultant shall, at the City's election, re-perform the non-conforming Services or refund the fees paid therefor.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation runs exclusively in one direction: only the Consultant warrants that it is duly authorized and empowered to enter the Agreement, leaving Columbia Capital Management without an equivalent representation it can rely upon if the Consultant later challenges enforceability or claims its execution was unauthorized. For Columbia Capital Management, this asymmetry creates a material enforcement risk — if a dispute arises, the absence of a mutual authority representation may complicate Columbia Capital Management's ability to hold the Consultant to its contractual obligations. Market-standard practice in Professional Services Agreements requires both parties to represent their respective authority to execute, deliver, and perform.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each of Consultant and Columbia Capital Management is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
